lessons.title: Near looks bigger
body: Perspective mimics a familiar visual cue: objects closer to the camera look larger. The camera projects a volume of 3D space onto the 2D image.
These two cubes have identical geometry. The mint cube is farther from the camera. Move it closer along positive Z and observe its apparent size grow. Its actual scale remains unchanged.
lessons.hint: Change only the Z position of other, not its scale.

quiz.question: In perspective, a closer object usually appears…
quiz.explanation: Perspective divides by depth, so distance affects apparent size.

lessons.title: Wide angle, narrow angle
body: A perspective camera’s fov is its vertical field of view, measured in degrees. A larger value fits more of the world into the image; a smaller value creates a tighter view.

Changing projection settings requires updateProjectionMatrix(). Without that update, the camera keeps using its previous projection. This is different from moving the camera: perspective relationships can change differently.
lessons.hint: Use degrees here. Unlike mesh rotation, fov does not use radians.

quiz.question: A larger field of view shows…
quiz.explanation: A wider lens includes a wider vertical angle.

lessons.title: What the camera cannot see
body: A camera draws only a bounded region. Surfaces nearer than near or farther than far are clipped. Our cube is around 8 units from the camera, beyond the current far plane.

Increasing far reveals it. Keep near above zero for perspective cameras, and avoid an unnecessarily huge gap between near and far: depth precision is finite and poor settings can produce flickering surfaces called z-fighting.

quiz.question: What happens beyond the far plane?
quiz.explanation: The far plane limits the visible depth range.

lessons.title: A view without perspective
body: An orthographic camera keeps apparent size independent of distance. It is useful for diagrams, CAD, isometric scenes, and some games. Its left, right, top, and bottom bounds define the visible volume.

Our useCamera helper switches the viewer’s active camera and keeps its aspect ratio responsive. Activate the prepared orthographic camera, then orbit around the two equal-size cubes and compare their projection.
lessons.task: Change selected = camera to selected = ortho before useCamera(selected).
lessons.hint: Edit the second assignment to selected. The helper makes that camera active.

quiz.question: Which projection preserves size regardless of depth?
quiz.explanation: Orthographic projection does not shrink objects as their depth increases.

lessons.title: Give the viewer control
body: OrbitControls moves a camera around a target. Dragging orbits, scrolling zooms, and right-dragging pans. Damping smooths movement, and requires controls.update() in the animation loop; the workspace handles that.

Controls can have distance and angle limits. Auto-rotation is useful for a product turntable. Enable it below, then drag the scene yourself. The control system continues to handle the camera while your objects remain still.
lessons.hint: Set autoRotate to true. autoRotateSpeed controls how quickly it turns.

quiz.question: What does OrbitControls usually move?
quiz.explanation: Orbit controls change the camera’s position and orientation around a target.
